feedback.problem:
Given the Cartesian equation $9x-3y+6=0$ of the plane $Π$, find an equation of $Π$ in the form $(r-p)\cdot n=0.$

feedback.worked_solution:
First, from the equation of the plane we get that the normal vector of $Π$ is $n=⟨9,-3,0⟩.$

Now, we solve the Cartesian equation of $Π$ for $y$:

$$
\begin{aligned}9x-3y+6 & =0 \\ -3y & =-9x-6 \\ y & =3x+2\end{aligned}
$$

If we put, say, $x=0$, we get $y=2.$ Hence, the point $P(0,2,0)$ lies on $Π.$ Note that the position vector of $P$ is $p=⟨0,2,0⟩.$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ (r-⟨0,2,0⟩)\cdot ⟨9,-3,0⟩ & =0.\end{aligned}
$$
